# Testament of Levi — 3
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Of all the Testaments, Levi's is the most visionary. He doesn't confess a sin — he describes a calling. Heaven opened to him. He was chosen.

**1** These are the words Levi left his sons: what they must do, and what would happen to them until the final judgment. He was healthy when he called them together — he knew he was dying because it had been shown to him.

**2** He said:

I was born in Haran. I came with my father to Shechem as a young man, about twenty years old. That was when Simeon and I took vengeance on Hamor for what they did to our sister Dinah.

**3** On the way back from that killing, I was in deep grief. I lay down and slept, and I had a vision — the same kind Abraham our father had seen.

**4** The heavens opened. An angel said: Levi, come up. **5** I went from the first heaven into the second, and between them I saw water hanging in the air. **6** And beyond that, a third heaven — far more brilliant, of incomprehensible height. **7** I asked the angel what this meant. He said: Don't be amazed yet — there are higher heavens still. You are standing near the LORD. You will be his servant. You will reveal his mysteries to humanity. You will announce the one who will redeem Israel. Through you and Judah, God will be seen among people.

**8** Then the angel opened the gate of heaven and I saw the holy temple — and on a throne of glory, the Most High. **9** He spoke to me: Levi, I give you the priesthood until I myself come and dwell in the middle of Israel.

**10** The angel brought me back down to earth and handed me a shield and a sword. He said: Now go and do what must be done at Shechem for Dinah. The LORD has sent me with you.

**11** So I killed Shechem. Simeon killed Hamor. Our brothers came in and finished the rest. **12** Our father Jacob heard about it and was furious — and grieved, because the Canaanites and the Perizzites were aware of what we'd done. He knew it would make things dangerous for us. We moved on and came to Bethel.

**13** At Bethel I had a second vision — seventy days after we arrived. Seven men dressed in white stood before me. They said: Levi, rise. Put on the priestly vestments.

**14** And one by one they dressed me. The robe of the priesthood. The crown of righteousness. The breastplate of understanding. The garment of truth. The plate of faith. The turban of a sign. The ephod of prophecy. **15** Each of the seven placed something on me. The first anointed me with oil and gave me the staff of judgment. The second washed me with pure water and fed me bread and wine — the most sacred things — and clothed me in a holy robe. The others added the linen, the girdle, the olive branch, the crown. The seventh placed the diadem of the high priesthood on my head and filled my hands with incense.

**16** They said: From this day forward, you and your descendants are priests of the LORD forever. **17** Your line will be divided into three offices. The first will be greatest of all. The second will be the continuing priesthood. The third will receive a new name — because a king will arise from Judah who will establish a new kind of priesthood, fashioned differently, for all peoples. And that one will be beloved like a prophet of the Most High, from the seed of Abraham.

**18** After the vision I went with Judah to see Isaac our grandfather. He blessed me according to everything I had seen in the visions. **19** And Isaac taught me the priestly law — sacrifices, burnt offerings, firstfruits, peace offerings — day after day, training me to serve before the LORD.

**20** Now I tell you, my sons, what I saw in those visions concerning the future of our people.

The angel showed me: Israel will be scattered. They will dishonor the law. They will turn away from the commandments. They will be given over to the nations.

**21** But then — a man will come who renews the law in the power of the Most High. You will call him a deceiver. He will not be a deceiver. He will be a new priest whom God himself appoints. **22** He will judge the earth in righteousness. His star will rise in heaven like a king's star, blazing knowledge like the sun blazes light. **23** He will be exalted across the whole world. He will shine on earth and strip away every darkness from under heaven. And there will be peace — everywhere.

**24** The heavens will rejoice in his days. The earth will be glad. The knowledge of the LORD will be poured over the whole earth like water filling the seas. And the angels of the presence of the Most High will be glad in him.

---
*End of Testament of Levi*
